subject: SOC 2 Type II — hosting scope questions (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)
messages:
From: Benjamin Stewart <benjamin.stewart@acmeinc.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmeinc.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — Redwood coverage for our hosting choices

Hi Nikhil,

We're in the middle of our procurement & InfoSec review and hit a couple of questions on Redwood's SOC 2 coverage that I hoped you could clarify quickly:

1) Audit period: we requested coverage for our onboarding window (audit period: 2025-09-01 — 2026-08-31). Do you have a Type II covering that window? If not, can you provide a bridge letter or attestation?

2) Scope: we plan to use a mixture of Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for our production inference and a Private/VPC deployment for a subset of regulated flows. Which hosting modes are covered by your SOC 2 Type II? Specifically:
  - If the runtime is deployed into our VPC (customer-managed runtime) but the Redwood control plane manages model versions and routing, is the deployment "in-scope" or are there carve-outs?
  - For Dedicated pools (Redwood-managed but single-tenant capacity), is that included in the standard report or treated separately?

3) Evidence requests: our auditors will want tenant mapping, change control logs for the audit period, and proof of key management (KMS/HSM) usage for customer keys. Can you produce those artifacts or confirm which are out of scope for private deployments?

I've attached our questionnaire (acme_security_questionnaire_20270615.xlsx) — could you confirm what you can supply by EOD Friday? If a bridge letter is needed, a draft would be helpful.

Thanks,
Ben
Benjamin Stewart

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — Redwood coverage for our hosting choices

Ben — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then specifics and next steps: 

Summary answers:
- Audit period: We have a SOC 2 Type II report covering 2025-09-01 through 2026-08-31 (attached).
- Dedicated pools: Included in our Type II when the customer has a Dedicated contract and we maintain tenant mapping / isolation evidence — we'll provide tenant mapping and pool allocation artifacts.
- Private/VPC: When runtime is deployed into a customer-managed VPC (or on-prem), certain infrastructure and physical access controls are out of scope for Redwood's hosted report. We can provide a bridge letter that delineates which controls remain our responsibility (control plane, model handling, logging we ingest) versus customer responsibility (host OS, hypervisor, network boundary, customer KMS).

What we're attaching / can provide quickly:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (full report for 2025-09-01 — 2026-08-31)
- Draft bridge letter that covers Private/VPC deployments and details required evidence for carve-ins (bridge_letter_hosted_dedicated_draft.docx)
- Tenant-mapping export for Dedicated pools (redacted) and change-control log extracts for the audit period (we'll pull these and send by Thursday).

Specifics on scope boundaries (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): fully in-scope for our SOC 2 Type II. Controls for network, host, patching, perimeter logging, and runtime are included.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Included when a Dedicated contract exists and the tenant mapping & allocation artifacts show the customer was assigned capacity within the audited period. We will provide: pool allocation CSV, control plane ACL snapshots, and autoscale/change audit entries.
- Private / VPC / On-prem deployments: Control-plane services we run (model registry, deployment orchestration, API keys issuance, audit logs captured by our control plane) remain in-scope for Redwood. Anything that runs inside the customer's VPC or on-premise host (host OS, customer-managed KMS keys, network ACLs) is out-of-scope for our Type II; where a customer requires coverage, we produce a bridge letter and list required evidence the customer must provide to their auditor (network diagrams, host patching records, HSM attestations).

Next steps / ask from you:
1) Confirm whether you plan to use Dedicated for the whole audit window or if Dedicated onboarding happened mid-period (that affects what we include in tenant mapping).
2) If you expect Private/VPC coverage in your audit, we'll send a bridge letter and a checklist of artifacts to collect.
3) I'll loop in our compliance team and Kimberly/Marissa to pull tenant mapping and change logs. Expect a follow-up by Thursday 6/17.

If helpful, we can do a 30-min call to walk through the bridge wording and artifact list.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Technical Sales, Redwood Inference
